GS.rationale: Goldman Sachs shows strong fundamental health and trajectory. Q1 2026 revenue of $17.23B and EPS of $17.55 represent robust YoY growth of +14.4% and +24.3% respectively, with QoQ acceleration of +13.5% and +43.3%. The firm just reported a record Q2 2026 EPS of $20.98, crushing consensus of $14.47 by 45%, with revenue of $20.34B up 39.4% YoY. This was driven by a 53% increase in Global Banking & Markets revenue and record assets under management exceeding $4 trillion. Net margin has improved to 29.9% and ROE to 14.7%, up from 12% a year ago. The franchise remains elite in investment banking and trading, with strategic focus on growing recurring fee-based asset and wealth management revenue. Valuation is moderate: P/E of 17.47x sits in the middle of its 14.5-19.6x 12-month range, while P/B of 2.57x is near the top of its 1.8-2.9x range. The stock has rallied +13.2% over the past quarter to $1,024.86, partially reflecting the strong Q2 beat. Near-term catalyst exists: the Q2 earnings beat on July 14 was massive and the stock jumped 9% the next day, but the stock has since pulled back from $1,140 to $1,025, suggesting the market may not have fully digested the earnings power. However, macro headwinds are notable: 10Y Treasury yields have risen to 4.68%, the yield curve has flattened (T10Y2Y at 0.45%), and geopolitical tensions with oil price volatility create uncertainty for capital markets activity. The operating cash flow of -$31.87B in Q1 2026 is a concern, though this is typical for large banks with volatile working capital. Overall, the fundamental trajectory is clearly positive with strong earnings momentum, but valuation is not cheap enough to warrant a higher score, and macro risks temper enthusiasm.
